summary: Compact ADC editing workspaces; Audit lifecycle, version Change Logs and controlled updates; Versioned first-party plugin standards, approval policy and developer SDK; Optional first-party plugin controls and cross-platform Relay source support; Bind MCP sessions to project credentials and correct Python indexing scope and argument flows; Unified interactive reporting workspace; Remove the user menu's green active border

Changed: Compact Constitution toolbars and collapse publication/import controls.
Place the Amendments change picker beside the editor and collapse baseline review, history and collection tools.
Separate product release history from request audit records and local unpublished work.
The developer kit remains a verified local candidate: GitHub workflow authorization and independent publication approvals are still required; no SDK release or runtime update has been published.
Automation, browser tasks, workflows, reports, notifications and evaluation retain their existing integration contracts behind optional-plugin host checks.
Cross-platform Relay release workflows require their platform signing and notarization prerequisites; source candidates do not imply published platform releases.
Merged Report and AI-First into one filter-driven workspace, retaining evidence/policy tools and legacy saved reports in collapsed sections.
Date/project/type/status/text filters apply before the bounded activity sample; current readiness is explicitly separate from historical activity.
The user menu button keeps its neutral border when a management page is active.
Added: Audit capacity and policy previews, confirmed persistent retention settings and bounded background cleanup.
System settings Change Logs, bundled release history and release-time change-note validation.
Online release checks and notifications, signed update manifests and administrator-confirmed host update requests.
English/Chinese plugin contract and independent exact-commit approval policy, with explicit trusted in-process boundaries.
Installable Python SDK with scaffolding, semantic/file validation, host adapter result contracts and deterministic non-overwriting packages.
Joint standards/SDK packaging and approval-gated provenance publication workflows; drafts and missing reviewer configuration do not count as formal approval.
Selectable first-party plugin packaging, administrator enable/install controls and focused plugin settings with execution-aware disable safeguards.
Linux tray and user-service packaging plus macOS CLI packaging, native credential backends and explicit session-only credential mode.
Local ECharts interactive charts with matching dark/light themes, evidence drill-down and snapshot-bound CSV/JSON exports.
Downloadable Mermaid-led PDF reports and diagram sources; PDF evidence is explicitly limited while CSV/JSON retain the complete generated snapshot.
Security: Keep audit deletion disabled until a policy is previewed and explicitly enabled.
Require trusted signed artifacts and an independently configured host executor before enabling installation; preserve existing ports and data.
Bind MCP SSE sessions to their database-verified project and exact credential; reject another project's or another token's messages before tool execution.
Require MCP Python SDK 1.30.0 or newer in the supported 1.x line, including session ownership and client transport fixes.
Fixed: Review fixes preserve ADC exemptions and CRLF snapshots, expose per-file collection review and include research-report conventions in generated templates.
Plugin selection survives leaner bundles; briefing holds execution leases and evaluation resumes pending Redis traces after restart.
Confirmed upgrades wait for audit cleanup and require request-specific drain receipts; reports stream bounded summary projections and reject oversized results.
Release publication rejects existing SDK tags, validates trusted workflow provenance and delays public image tag promotion until release gates pass.
Keep Python nested function identities, imports, calls and variable flows within their lexical scopes rather than merging same-named closures or attributing nested bodies to their parent.
Preserve positional, keyword and repeated argument dependencies when building cross-function data-flow edges; do not invent bindings for unresolved argument expansion.
